title: Getting started with WeGrowHealthR
text: wgh_add_zscores() adds height--age (haz), weight--age (waz) BMI--age (baz) z-scores. reference = "" (default) uses 2006 Child Growth Standards 60 months 2007 Growth Reference 60 months, restricted tails weight BMI. values agree anthro anthroplus packages. reference = "cdc" uses CDC 2000 growth charts (2 20 years). percentiles = TRUE adds matching percentiles. two references differ, BMI, built different populations periods. Weight--age defined 10 years CDC 2 years, cells missing. single values, wgh_zscore() takes measurement, age, sex indicator. wgh_compare_references() shows several versions side side, helps need explain two software packages disagree: columns value restricted tails (), plain LMS value without (who_plain_lms), symmetric approximation, CDC value, anthroplus value package installed. can also give reference data frame columns sex, age (years), L, M S (optionally indicator), example national growth reference.

title: Getting started with WeGrowHealthR
text: wgh_prevalence() estimates prevalence indicator, share category status variable, confidence intervals. sets groups. categorical status, method = "sison_glaz" gives simultaneous intervals categories together, Ho et al. (2026, Sci Rep 16:7515). row gives number visits (n), number condition (cases), prevalence percent interval. trend calendar time tested Cochran-Armitage test: small p-value says prevalence changes steadily across years. Repeated visits child independent, formal inference trends use GEE models wgh_gee_trend(), trend flows apply (see vignette("trends-malnutrition")).

title: SITAR growth curves and the pubertal growth spurt
text: SITAR (SuperImposition Translation Rotation) describes every child’s height curve one mean curve shifted size (, cm), timing (b, years, negative means earlier) intensity (c, log scale, positive means faster, intense spurt). wgh_fit_sitar() wraps sitar::sitar(): df flexibility mean spline (4 5 usual), fixed random choose effects ("+ b + c", "+ b + c + d" extended model), age_range ages used min_visits visits needed per child, max_children limits number children (set run mode). never stops failed fit. Instead keeps error, competing models can compared, retries one fewer degree freedom. printout shows number children visits, population APHV PHV, diagnostics: whether fit converged, whether velocity curve turns negative tails, residual SD.  plot() takes type = "velocity", "height" "", trim show_data, plus shared display options.
code: boys <- v[v$sex == "Male" & v$age >= 6 & v$age <= 18, ] fit_m <- wgh_fit_sitar(boys, df = 5, age_range = c(6, 18)) #> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 3643 children (run mode "dev"). fit_m #> <wgh_sitar> "6-18 a+b+c": 3990 visits from 1000 children, df = 5 #> Population APHV 12.03 y, PHV 10.12 cm/y #> # A tibble: 1 x 15 #>   model    converged n_children    AIC    BIC sigma  RMSE  sd_a  sd_b   sd_c  sd_d min_velocity_tail #>   <chr>    <lgl>          <int>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>             <dbl> #> 1 6-18 a+~ TRUE            1000 14992. 15087. 0.527 0.360  4.47 0.464 0.0715    NA             0.146 #> # i 3 more variables: max_re_corr <dbl>, APHV <dbl>, PHV <dbl> plot(fit_m, type = "both", line_width = 1.2)

title: SITAR growth curves and the pubertal growth spurt
text: Two checks matter using estimates. wgh_check_identifiable() flags random effects almost perfectly correlated, sign model separate . wgh_sitar_select() compares candidate specifications BIC, positive velocity tails stable APHV PHV, picks one stated rule (procedure used girls [1]). Read sel$reason using selected model. , subsample 1,000 girls development mode, candidate meets every criterion, function keeps first model says candidate failed. full cohort (wgh_config("publication")) candidates may converge. none acceptable, show mean curve ages enough data report reason results.

text: conditional growth references (vignette("growth-distributions")) predict several quantiles later height--age child. second study asked whether features drive median, lower upper predictions. linear quantile model independent features, SHAP values exact simple: coefficient times centred feature value, interaction terms shared equally features. wgh_shap_interaction() computes . Baseline HAZ dominates quantiles, baseline age contributes upper prediction lower one. features shape two ends child’s expected range differently, single mean model show.
code: cp <- wgh_conditional_panel(v, window = c(5, 10), targets = 12) z <- cp[cp$sex == "Female" & complete.cases(cp[, c("baseline_haz", "baseline_baz", "baseline_age")]), ] q10 <- quantreg::rq(target ~ baseline_haz * baseline_baz + baseline_age, tau = 0.1, data = z) q90 <- quantreg::rq(target ~ baseline_haz * baseline_baz + baseline_age, tau = 0.9, data = z) s10 <- wgh_shap_interaction(coef(q10), z, z) s90 <- wgh_shap_interaction(coef(q90), z, z) rbind(q10 = colMeans(abs(s10$S)), q90 = colMeans(abs(s90$S))) #>     baseline_haz baseline_baz baseline_age #> q10    0.3650404   0.04197381   0.08772003 #> q90    0.4353093   0.02445454   0.21324733

what: 4. A mixed model of the trajectory
title: Prepubertal BMI and the height trajectory
text: group comparisons use cross-sections. linear mixed model uses every visit every child. wgh_fit_lmm() fits HAZ natural spline age interacting index category, fixed site effect, random intercept slope age within child (random = "(1 + age_c | id)", age centred 10 years). marginal R2 variance explained fixed effects conditional R2 adds child random effects. large difference , high ICC, means variation HAZ stable differences children, expected height. wgh_contrasts() reads model stated ages compares categories pairwise (emmeans): row difference mean HAZ two categories one age, Holm-adjusted p-value. girls, obesity puberty taller normal BMI 8 years, advantage shrinks 12 years, turns deficit 16 years. pattern earlier puberty earlier end growth.

text: Population APHV PHV read SITAR mean velocity curve within fitted age range. Individual APHV PHV computed children random effects exact SITAR relationship $$APHV_i = x_0 + b_0 + b_i + (APHV - x_0 - b_0) e^{-c_i}, \quad PHV_i = PHV e^{c_i},$$ \(x_0\) age offset \(b_0\) fixed timing effect. replaces per-child prediction loop Book 1 Chapter 9 approximation APHV + b_i used original code SITAR pubertal spurt study (Ho et al. 2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358986), ignores intensity. title: Create a validated growth data object — wgh_data
text: data data frame one row per child visit. id, sex Child identifier sex (common coding "Male"/"Female", "M"/"F" 1/2). age Age measurement (optional dob date given). dob, date Date birth date measurement. Dates, character strings format readable .Date() (see date_format). height, weight Height cm weight kg (optional). site, year Recruitment site calendar (school) year (optional). year given date , calendar year measurement used. bmi Optional existing BMI column. absent height weight present, BMI computed. age_unit Unit age: "years" (default), "months" "days". age_from "auto", "age" (use age column ) "dates" (always compute age dob date). date_format Format passed .Date() dates stored text, example "%d/%m/%Y". default reads ISO dates ("2024-09-15"). check TRUE (default), run plausibility checks report .

title: Create a validated growth data object — wgh_data

title: Create a validated growth data object — wgh_data
text: Age can given directly (age) computed date birth (dob) date measurement (date). age_from = "auto" (default) supplied age column used missing ages filled dates. age_from = "dates" age always computed dates, accurate choice dates recorded. text: wgh_simulate() generates cohort children followed annual school health examinations. child's height curve SITAR-type transformation (size, timing intensity) Preece-Baines mean curve, every child's velocity positive every age. latent adiposity score shifts timing, size intensity, drives BMI BMI--age reference makes attendance informative. Children belong latent phenotypes. output separates real study see (visits) simulation knows (truth_child, truth_visit).

title: Simulate a longitudinal school health cohort — wgh_simulate
